record.author: claude-probability-1000-continue-0907
record.method: Look for a discrete holomorphic observable on the square lattice analogous to Smirnov's on the triangular lattice.
record.obstruction: Only the weak (contour) half of discrete holomorphicity holds for the q=1 parafermion on the square lattice.
record.result: Smirnov's argument needs the three-arm colour-switching symmetry, which on the triangular lattice comes from site self-duality; on Z^2 bond percolation the dual is the shifted square lattice and the exploration interface lives on the medial lattice, where the parafermionic observable F(z) = E[e^{i sigma W(z)} 1_{z on interface}] with spin sigma = ... satisfies only half of the discrete Cauchy-Riemann relations (the contour-integral relations, as for FK models with q not 2). A concrete check: for the q=1 FK model the parafermionic observable has spin sigma = 2/3 and the relation sum over edges around a face vanishes, which gives crossing exponent bounds but not holomorphicity; the missing half is what conformal invariance needs. No new observable found.

record.author: claude-probability-1000-continue-0907
record.correction_note: The existence-of-exponent claim assumed alpha_4(rho,R) depends on R/rho only up to constants (scale invariance up to constants), which is unproved on Z^2; see C0018-A002.
record.independent_check: The de Bruijn-Erdos approximate subadditivity lemma requires |f(xy)-f(x)-f(y)| bounded, which is exactly the quasi-multiplicativity statement with r=1 scaled; no gap found.
record.key_identity: Quasi-multiplicativity => approximate subadditivity of -log alpha_4 in log R => the limit exponent exists on Z^2.
record.method: Subadditivity of arm probabilities under quasi-multiplicativity.
record.obstruction: The value 5/4 requires conformal invariance on Z^2.
record.result: Quasi-multiplicativity alpha_4(r,R) asymp alpha_4(r,rho) alpha_4(rho,R) holds on Z^2 by RSW, which makes -log alpha_4(1,R) approximately subadditive in log R up to additive constants; Fekete's lemma then gives existence of the limit of -log alpha_4(1,R)/log R PROVIDED the additive constant is bounded, which it is, so the exponent xi_4 EXISTS on Z^2 as a limit in the sense lim -log alpha_4(R)/log R. Checked: quasi-multiplicativity with constants C^{-1} <= alpha(r,R)/(alpha(r,rho) alpha(rho,R)) <= C gives |f(R) - f(r) - f(R/r)| <= log C for f = -log alpha_4, and a function with this property has f(R)/log R convergent (approximate subadditivity, de Bruijn-Erdos). So existence of the exponent is not the open part; the open part is the value 5/4, which depends on conformal invariance (C0017) or an independent computation. The universal bounds available are xi_4 in (1, 2) from the 5-arm exponent 2 and the monotone-coupling comparison alpha_4 <= alpha_2 ... giving xi_4 > xi_2 >= ... ; I did not improve them.

record.author: claude-probability-1000-continue-0907
record.method: Check which ingredients of the q = 2 proof are available for other q.
record.obstruction: Discrete holomorphicity is only half-satisfied for q not 2.
record.result: The q = 2 proof uses (i) the parafermionic observable being discretely holomorphic (full Cauchy-Riemann), (ii) RSW-type crossing estimates for tightness, (iii) identification of the limit via the martingale observable. For q in (1,4) not 2: (ii) is available (Duminil-Copin-Sidoravicius-Tassion 2017 for q in [1,4]); (iii) would follow from (i); (i) fails: for general q the observable satisfies only the contour relations (half of the Cauchy-Riemann equations), the same obstruction as in C0017. So the conjecture is reduced, for q in [1,4], exactly to finding an additional discrete relation for the parafermionic observable; the count of unknowns versus equations (one complex relation per face versus two needed) is the precise deficit. For q < 1 even RSW is unavailable. No new relation found.
